```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

An R language wrapper around [CO-OPS](https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/) handy [API](https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/prod/). While throughput is throttled, it is an easy way to gather tide and current data including observations.

> Someday we'll add access to the [metadata API](https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/mdapi/prod/#intro)

# Requirements

+ [R v4.2+](https://www.r-project.org/)
+ [rlang](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rlang)
+ [dplyr](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=dplyr)
+ [readr](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=readr)
+ [httr](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=httr)

# Installation

```
remotes::install_github("BigelowLab/coops")
```

# Usage

We don't provide any information on how to use the API, we simply wrap the API call in R for easy access.  Study the [API description](https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/prod/) for argument options. Decoding API responses is also not handled by this package, but you can learn more about the responses [here](https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/prod/responseHelp.html).

We set the default response type to CSV (data frames), but for many calls you can request XML or JSON.

Below is an example where request hourly tide hight for a year at the Portland Maine (8418150) tide gage. 

```{r query}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(coops)
  library(dplyr)
  library(patchwork)
})

x = query_coops(station = "8418150", # Portland Maine
                begin_date = as.Date("2020-01-01"),
                end_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),
                product = "hourly_height") |>
  glimpse()
```

More complex data can be obtained using `station_high_low()` which requests observed and predicted high and low maximums.  Both the observed height and time of the tidal maximum (minimum) can be quite different than the predicted values. We have a function that requests both observed and predicted heights,

```{r hilo}
hilo = station_high_low(station = "8418150",
                     begin_date = as.Date("1990-01-01"),
                     end_Date = as.Date("2000-01-01")) |>
  glimpse()
```

We interpolate the high/low maxima/mimima with`station_interpolate()` which examines the departure of the observed from the predicted. 

```{r hilo_interp}
interp_hilo = station_interpolate(hilo) |>
  glimpse()
```

And a plot...

```{r hilo_interp_plot}
plot_hilo(interp_hilo) |>
  wrap_plots(ncol = 1)
```
